title: One-time transfer of Schedule III-V prescription information for refill purposes
rule_summary: Transfer of original prescription information for a controlled substance listed in Schedule III, IV or V for the purpose of refill dispensing is permissible between pharmacies ON A ONE-TIME BASIS ONLY; pharmacies electronically sharing a real-time, online database may instead transfer up to the maximum refills permitted by law and the prescriber's authorization. The transfer must be communicated directly between two licensed pharmacists, the transferring pharmacist must void and annotate the original record, and the receiving pharmacist must record the required transfer data. The procedure is permissible only if allowable under existing State or other applicable law, and it moves the prescription without creating new refill authority or restarting the six-month issue-date clock.
exam_relevance: Tests whether a candidate applies the federal one-time transfer limit to a Schedule III-V refill transfer instead of stopping at a state rule that requires pharmacies to transfer on patient request.

authority.name: Transfer between pharmacies of prescription information for Schedules III, IV, and V controlled substances for refill purposes

numeric_facts.fact: Permitted transfers of Schedule III-V prescription information for refill purposes
numeric_facts.conditions: One-time basis only, unless the pharmacies electronically share a real-time, online database

exceptions: Pharmacies electronically sharing a real-time, online database may transfer up to the maximum refills permitted by law and the prescriber's authorization.
The transfer procedure is permissible only if allowable under existing State or other applicable law.
common_confusions: Treating a state duty to transfer on patient request as removing the federal one-time transfer limit.
Confusing this refill-purpose transfer rule with the separate one-time transfer of an unfilled electronic controlled prescription.
Assuming a transfer creates new refill authority or restarts the six-month issue-date clock.
